name: Brimhaven Agility Arena
notes: Tickets buy Agility xp in bulk; the rate climbs toward 50k by level 40

name: Agility Pyramid
notes: Slower, but the only course that pays you while you run it

name: Wilderness Agility Course
notes: Fastest in this bracket, but player killers camp the obstacles. Bring nothing you mind losing.

name: Hallowed Sepulchre (floor 1)
notes: Requires Sins of the Father; the safe answer to the same bracket as the Wilderness course

name: Seers' Village rooftop
notes: Marks of Grace toward the graceful outfit

name: Pollnivneach rooftop
notes: Marks of Grace toward the graceful outfit

name: Hallowed Sepulchre (floors 3-4)
notes: Reaches roughly 80k once floor 4 opens at 77

name: Prifddinas rooftop
notes: Requires Song of the Elves

name: Rellekka rooftop
notes: Marks of Grace toward the graceful outfit

name: Hallowed Sepulchre (floor 5)
notes: Fastest Agility in the game and entirely safe

name: Ardougne rooftop
notes: Best rooftop rate; the Ardougne hard diary speeds it up further

name: Pickpocketing men, farmers and master farmers
notes: Quests skip most of this bracket outright

name: Stealing from Aldarin villa chests
notes: Bring lockpicks and stamina potions

name: Blackjacking bandits (Pollnivneach)
notes: Very click-intensive; the rate more than doubles by level 65

name: Stealing artefacts (Port Piscarilius)
notes: Needs Piscarilius favour; far calmer than blackjacking

name: Pickpocketing Knights of Ardougne
notes: Safe and low-setup. Over 55-99: ~200 dodgy necklaces, ~16k hitpoints healed, ~7.6M coins.

name: Blackjacking menaphite thugs
notes: Fastest safe method outside the Wilderness, at high click intensity

name: Pickpocketing vyres (Darkmeyer)
notes: Requires Sins of the Father; good profit alongside the xp

name: Rogues' Castle chests
notes: The fastest Thieving there is. Player killers camp the castle, and you lose what you carry.

name: Pyramid Plunder
notes: Nearly as fast as Rogues' Castle with no PvP exposure at all

name: Quests and allotment runs
notes: Quests cover much of it; allotments fill the rest until oak trees open at 15.

name: Herb runs
notes: Far less xp than a tree run, but among the best passive income in the game.

name: Tree runs (regular, fruit and hardwood trees)
notes: The best Farming xp there is, a few minutes of clicking per run. Regular trees: oak 15, willow 30, maple 45, yew 60, magic 75. Fruit trees from 27: apple 27, banana 33, orange 39, curry 42, pineapple 51, papaya 57, palm 68, dragonfruit 81. Hardwood trees on Fossil Island from 35, calquat 72 and celastrus 85 along the way.

name: Low Level Alchemy
notes: Stationary and cheap; the standard way through the 20s and 30s

name: Superheat Item
notes: Gives Smithing xp at the same time, but you pay for the ore

name: Tele-alching at Camelot
notes: Alch between teleports; profitable and needs no combat

name: High Level Alchemy (passive)
notes: Done alongside another activity rather than as a session of its own

name: Ice Bursting maniacal monkeys
notes: Requires Monkey Madness II; roughly 400k once Ice Barrage unlocks at 94

name: Ice Bursting zombie pirates
notes: As fast as maniacal monkeys, and it pays for itself. You are a target the whole time.

name: Stun-alching
notes: Fastest non-combat Magic, at a punishing click rate

name: Plank Make
notes: Near-AFK and profitable; requires Lunar Diplomacy

name: Smithing bronze through steel at an anvil
notes: Rate climbs steeply as better bars unlock

name: Giants' Foundry
notes: Requires Sleeping Giants; low cost and low attention

name: Blast Furnace (iron through rune bars)
notes: Slower than gold but turns a profit instead of costing

name: Dart tips and nails
notes: Near-zero attention; usually breaks even

name: Steel cannonballs
notes: The AFK option — slow, but you can run it while doing something else

name: Blast Furnace (gold bars, goldsmith gauntlets)
notes: By far the fastest Smithing; needs goldsmith gauntlets, ice gloves and Family Crest

name: Dwarf multicannon on ogres or similar
notes: Fastest option before chinning unlocks

name: Gemstone crab
notes: Fully idle; far slower than chinning but costs nothing and needs no attention

name: Chinning maniacal monkeys (grey chinchompas)
notes: Requires Monkey Madness II chapter II; chins are consumed, so this is expensive

name: Chinning maniacal monkeys (red chinchompas)
notes: Expensive — budget for the chins before you start

name: Chinning maniacal monkeys (black chinchompas)
notes: The fastest xp/hr in the game, priced accordingly. Near 1M/hr at 99 with Rigour and void.

name: Nightmare Zone (venator bow)
notes: Largely AFK, and a fraction of the cost of chinning

name: Venator bow at maniacal monkeys
notes: Cheaper alternative to chins at the same spot

name: Iron ore (power mining)
notes: Drop the ore rather than banking it; Varrock armour helps

name: Motherlode Mine
notes: Low attention, and pays in nuggets and Prospector pieces. Reaches ~62k with upgrades.

name: Gem rocks (Shilo Village)
notes: Requires the medium Karamja diary; the gems are worth real money

name: 3-tick granite power-mining
notes: Requires precise drop-and-reclick timing every game tick; very click intensive

name: Calcified rocks (Lovakengj)
notes: Requires Lovakengj favour; the ore feeds the Blast Mine minigame itself

name: Crashed stars
notes: Very low effort; stardust charges the celestial ring

name: Volcanic Mine
notes: Group minigame requiring Bone Voyage; fastest normal-pace Mining

name: Blast Mine
notes: Profitable solo minigame; needs dynamite, a chisel and a tinderbox

name: Amethyst
notes: Slow but profitable and nearly AFK

name: Cutting gems (sapphire through diamond)
notes: Rate roughly doubles as better gems unlock; a jeweller's chisel adds another ~10%

name: Crafting battlestaves
notes: Fast and close to break-even if you alch the staves

name: Superglass Make
notes: Requires Lunar Diplomacy; profitable and calmer than d'hide

name: Dragonhide bodies
notes: Fastest normal-pace Crafting; a costume needle removes the thread juggling

name: 1.5-tick teaks (Fossil Island)
notes: Tick-perfect chopping, and the fastest Woodcutting there is. Reaches ~235k by 99.

name: Teak trees (regular pace)
notes: Solid through the mid game; falls off past 65 without tick manipulation

name: Maple trees
notes: The Kandarin medium diary improves this

name: Blisterwood tree
notes: No banking at all — the logs are consumed as you chop

name: Sulliuscep (Fossil Island)
notes: Needs Bone Voyage, and you walk a six-spot cycle across the Tar Swamp

name: Camphor trees (The Great Conch)
notes: Needs 45 Sailing and Troubled Tortugans started; a plain tree, no cycle to walk

name: Bloodwood trees
notes: Fastest without tick manipulation, but a two-tick cycle across three trees to reach it; needs The Blood Moon Rises

name: Engorged bloodwood tree
notes: The calm way to tap bloodwood: one tree, far less input, roughly half the rate

name: Ironwood trees (Sunbleak Island)
notes: Needs 72 Sailing; a steady rate for very little input - each tree lasts four minutes

name: Redwood trees
notes: Slower than bloodwood but completely AFK-friendly

name: Rosewood trees (Drumstick Isle)
notes: Needs 79 Sailing; drop the logs, there is no bank on the isle

name: Fly fishing (trout and salmon)
notes: Rate climbs toward 50k by the top of the bracket

name: Drift net fishing (Fossil Island)
notes: Trains Hunter at the same time; requires Bone Voyage

name: Barbarian Fishing
notes: Passive Agility and Strength xp alongside the Fishing

name: Barbarian Fishing (3-tick)
notes: Tick-perfect swapping between fishing and a second action

name: 2-tick harpooning (swordfish and tuna)
notes: Fastest Fishing in the game with a crystal harpoon

name: Leechfin fishing
notes: Requires The Blood Moon Rises; fastest normal-pace Fishing but very click heavy

name: Minnows
notes: Profitable, and needs the full angler's outfit

name: Dark crabs
notes: Taken for the profit, not the xp. You can be killed for the catch.

name: Low-level monsters (chickens, cows, Al Kharid warriors)
notes: Quests skip most of this bracket

name: Sand or ammonite crabs
notes: Fully AFK — the default when you want to do something else at the same time

name: Gemstone crab (Tlati Rainforest)
notes: Infinite health and low accuracy, so no food is needed

name: Slayer tasks
notes: Slower per hour, but it trains Slayer at the same time and pays for itself in drops

name: Sulphur naguas (Neypotzli)
notes: Requires 48 Slayer; restores prayer and the drops are worth keeping

name: Nightmare Zone
notes: The most AFK method in the game — minutes between clicks

name: Maniacal monkeys (Ape Atoll)
notes: Requires Monkey Madness II; prayer potion drops sustain Piety

notes: Quests skip most of this bracket

name: Comes naturally from any combat training
notes: Not trained directly — gained automatically from Attack/Strength/Defence/Ranged/Magic combat xp

name: Burying bones / Ectofuntus
notes: Quests cover most of this bracket faster than burying does

name: Gilded altar with dragon bones
notes: Needs 75 Construction and your own or a friend's altar; the standard safe method

name: Libation bowl with blessed bone shards
notes: Slightly cheaper than a gilded altar, at the cost of preparing the shards first

name: Chaos Temple altar
notes: Half the bone cost, from a 50% save chance. Bring one inventory at a time and expect to die.

name: Gilded altar with superior dragon bones
notes: The fastest Prayer in the game and the most expensive by a wide margin

name: Karambwan at the Hosidius kitchen
notes: Requires Tai Bwo Wannai Trio; the kitchen's burn reduction does the work

name: 1-tick karambwan
notes: Tick-perfect cooking; the fastest Cooking in the game, near 1M/hr by level 99

name: Cooking lobsters
notes: Cheap, and profitable at most prices

name: Jugs of wine
notes: Fastest normal-pace Cooking, and wine never burns

name: Cooking anglerfish
notes: Fast and turns a profit rather than costing one

name: Darts
notes: Zero-time training — fletch while doing something else entirely

name: Oak and willow longbows
notes: Roughly break-even

name: Battlestaves (celastrus bark)
notes: Fastest Fletching for most of the game; the bark comes from your own farming patch

name: Yew longbows (u)
notes: Cheaper than battlestaves and can turn a profit strung

name: Redwood shields
notes: Fastest late-game option

name: Burning willow and maple logs
notes: Burn in a line next to a bank

name: Wintertodt
notes: Pays in supply crates and pyromancer pieces and gives passive Woodcutting xp; ~320k by level 99

name: Burning magic logs
notes: Much faster than Wintertodt, but you are buying every log

name: Burning redwood logs
notes: Fastest Firemaking in the game, and the most expensive

name: Attack and antipoison potions
notes: Druidic Ritual unlocks the skill at level 3 and quests cover much of the rest of this bracket

name: Prayer potions
notes: Profitable as well as fast

name: Mastering Mixology
notes: Requires Children of the Sun; slower, but it pays in reward points rather than costing gp

name: Stamina / extended antifire with tick manipulation
notes: Tick-perfect mixing; the fastest Herblore short of the very top potions

name: Tasks from your assigned Slayer master
notes: Not an hourly grind. Better masters (Nieve, Duradel) unlock better tasks and more points.

name: Talisman tiaras
notes: The grind, if you would rather not quest — expensive and click-intensive

name: Quests
notes: These cover 1-32 between them. What Lies Below adds 8,000 more at 35.

name: Lava runes
notes: No pouches yet — a binding necklace guarantees the combination

name: Lava runes
notes: With small and medium pouches

name: Guardians of the Rift
notes: Passive Mining and Crafting xp, plus the Raiments of the Eye and the colossal pouch

name: Ourania (ZMI) altar
notes: No quest requirements, profitable, and no combat risk; climbs steeply once you have pouches

name: Lava runes
notes: With small, medium and large pouches

name: Lava runes
notes: With the giant pouch; a colossal pouch is worth about 2k/hr more here

name: Blood runes (Arceuus)
notes: Best gp/hr in the skill, with passive Mining and Crafting xp

name: Double astral runes
notes: Requires Lunar Diplomacy; strong profit alongside the xp

name: Lava runes
notes: With a colossal pouch from Guardians of the Rift — the pouch matters more than the level

name: Bird house runs (Fossil Island)
notes: Passive: a few minutes every 50. Run it alongside other training; scales with birdhouse tier.

name: Box trapping (red crabs)
notes: Two traps until level 40

name: Box trapping (embertailed jerboas)
notes: Three traps from level 40

name: Deadfall trapping (razor-backed kebbits)
notes: Fastest safe method for most of the mid game and far faster than box trapping

name: Carnivorous (red) chinchompas
notes: The safe alternative to black chins. Needs Eagles' Peak; faster once five traps unlock at 80.

name: Hunter rumours — Expert tier (Hunters' Guild)
notes: Safe, varied, and pays in hunter loot sacks. Novice and Adept open at 46 and 57 but are slower.

name: Black chinchompas
notes: You lose everything you carry on death. Rates climb past 200k once five traps unlock at 80.

name: Box trapping (rainbow crabs)
notes: Five traps from level 80

name: Herbiboar (Fossil Island)
notes: Also yields herbs; no traps or supplies needed

name: Carnivorous chinchompas with tick manipulation
notes: Tick-perfect trap resetting; roughly the same rate as black chinchompas without the Wilderness

name: Hunter rumours — Master tier (Hunters' Guild)
notes: Requires At First Light; the fastest safe method in the skill

name: Planks, crude chairs and oak repair benches
Oak larders
notes: A butler from level 40 does the banking for you

name: Mahogany tables
notes: Needs a demon butler; among the most expensive training in the game

name: Oak dungeon doors
notes: The budget option — meaningfully cheaper than mahogany for a modest rate loss

name: Gnome benches (superior garden)
notes: Fastest xp/hr of any skill in the game; needs a demon butler

name: Pandemonium (quest)
notes: Sailing cannot be trained before it: the quest teaches the skill and gives you a raft

name: Sea charting, with courier tasks on the way
notes: Chart every sea you can reach and carry cargo between the ports as you go. Prying Times at 12 and Current Affairs at 22 unlock more charting tasks. Always trim your sails.

name: Shipwreck salvaging (small and fisherman's wrecks)
notes: Slow this early, but nearly hands-off. Fisherman's wrecks from 26 roughly double it.

name: Sea charting and courier tasks
notes: The calmer way to 45. Crab Quest at 40 gives 10,000 xp, and charting alone carries you to about level 50.

name: Barracuda Trials: The Tempor Tantrum
notes: The fastest repeatable xp from 30. About 19k an hour at Swordfish rank; work up to Shark and Marlin.

name: Shipwreck salvaging (barracuda wrecks)
notes: Much faster from 42 with a salvaging station; a second hook adds about a third

name: Barracuda Trials: The Tempor Tantrum
notes: At Marlin rank, about 24k an hour

name: Courier tasks: Summer Shore route
notes: Needs Troubled Tortugans. About nine deliveries an hour of 2,000-2,500 xp each; bring 20,000 coins to recover your boat.

name: Shipwreck salvaging (large wrecks)
notes: With one mithril hook; about 25k an hour with two

name: Barracuda Trials: The Jubbly Jive
notes: About 65k an hour at Swordfish rank; work up to Shark and Marlin

name: Barracuda Trials: The Jubbly Jive
notes: At Marlin rank, about 89k an hour

name: Courier tasks: Rellekka route
notes: Rises to about 99k an hour once Etceteria opens at 65, depending on the tasks on offer

name: Shipwreck salvaging (pirate wrecks)
notes: Two hooks and a crewmate on one of them

name: Courier tasks: Prifddinas route
notes: Needs Song of the Elves. Aldarin, Port Tyras and Deepfin Point to Prifddinas.

name: Barracuda Trials: The Gwenith Glide
notes: About 114k an hour at Swordfish rank; work up to Shark and Marlin

name: Shipwreck salvaging (mercenary wrecks)
notes: Two adamant hooks; 65-70k an hour with rune

name: Barracuda Trials: The Gwenith Glide
notes: At Marlin rank, about 184k an hour; a crystal extractor and a rosewood hull push it past 200k

name: Courier tasks: Lunar Isle route
notes: Round trips to Lunar Isle, up to 160k an hour; five tasks at once from level 84

name: Shipwreck salvaging (Fremennik and merchant wrecks)
notes: Two rune hooks; merchant wrecks from 87 reach 80-95k an hour with dragon hooks
